decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display sits at the core of the cardboard catalog and costs little to keep, though the 2022 rise in paper and energy costs and its absence from the website in 2020 to 2021 make some pruning of variants more likely.
The pegboard-back display serves hook-merchandise customers on existing cardboard lines, but the cost pressure in 2022 may prompt problemistic search that trims niche variants.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a staple format for consumer brands and fits the one-stop model, so it most likely still meets aspirations despite the cost pressure.
The eighth-pallet format complements the quarter-pallet line for smaller placements at low extra cost, though its overlap with that line makes it a candidate if the range is consolidated.

The wooden pallet lies furthest from the cardboard core and its evidence is still uncertain, but a large firm's slack and retailers' demand for durable, sustainable displays favour carrying it a little longer.
